questions.question: A car travels from Kanpur to Delhi at an average speed of 60 km/h and returns at an average speed of 90 km/h. Find the average speed of the car in the whole journey.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed from Kanpur to Delhi = 60 km/h.

Speed from Delhi to Kanpur = 90 km/h.

**Formula Used:**

Average speed = Total distance travelled / Total Time

**Calculation:**

Let the distance between Kanpur and Delhi be d km.

Time taken from Kanpur to Delhi = d / 60

Time taken from Delhi to Kanpur = d / 90

questions.question:
A shopkeeper declares the following three schemes of discounts. Which scheme is most beneficial to a customer?

A. Buy 25 items and get 30 of the same items

B. Two successive discounts of 12% and 18%

C. Two successive equal discounts of 15%
questions.solution:
**Given:**

We have three schemes of discounts. We need to determine which scheme is most beneficial to the customer:

A. Buy 25 items and get 30 of the same items

B. Two successive discounts of 12% and 18%

C. Two successive equal discounts of 15%

**Concept Used:**

To compare these schemes, we will calculate the final price for each scheme, assuming the cost of one item is ₹100.

**Scheme A:**

If you buy 25 items, you get 30 items. So, the total number of items you get is 30, and you pay for only 25 items.

For 25 items at ₹100 each, the total cost = 25 × ₹100 = ₹2500.

The effective cost per item is = ₹2500 / 30 = ₹83.33.

**Scheme B:**

For two successive discounts of 12% and 18%, the price is first reduced by 12%, then the new price is reduced by 18%.

The original price of one item is ₹100.

After the first discount of 12%, the price becomes:

₹100 - 12% of ₹100 = ₹100 - ₹12 = ₹88.

After the second discount of 18%, the price becomes:

₹88 - 18% of ₹88 = ₹88 - ₹15.84 = ₹72.16.

**Scheme C:**

For two successive equal discounts of 15%, the price is first reduced by 15%, then the new price is reduced by 15% again.

The original price of one item is ₹100.

After the first discount of 15%, the price becomes:

₹100 - 15% of ₹100 = ₹100 - ₹15 = ₹85.

After the second discount of 15%, the price becomes:

₹85 - 15% of ₹85 = ₹85 - ₹12.75 = ₹72.25.

**Comparison:**

Scheme A: Effective price per item = ₹83.33

Scheme B: Final price per item = ₹72.16

Scheme C: Final price per item = ₹72.25

**Conclusion:**

Scheme B is the most beneficial for the customer, as it offers the lowest final price of ₹72.16 per item.

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum of money at the rate of 5% per annum for 9 years is ₹1,260. At what rate of interest can the same amount of interest be received on the same sum after 6 years?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the Principal (P) and Simple Interest (I) are the same in both cases, the product of Rate (R) and Time (T) must be constant.

⇒ R₁ × T₁ = R₂ × T₂

⇒ 5 × 9 = R₂ × 6

⇒ 45 = 6 × R₂

⇒ R₂ = 45 ÷ 6 = 7.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1: Interest (I) = ₹1,260, Rate (R₁) = 5%, Time (T₁) = 9 years

Case 2: Interest (I) = ₹1,260, Time (T₂) = 6 years, Principal (P) is same as Case 1.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (I) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1826f837d231d363c165f0e5b9634a802d6cc432d8c5903420b89cfbc58d6889.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1,260 = (P × 5 × 9) ÷ 100

⇒ 1,260 = (P × 45) ÷ 100

⇒ P = (1,260 × 100) ÷ 45

⇒ P = 28 × 100 = ₹2,800

Now, using this Principal for the second case:

⇒ 1,260 = (2,800 × R₂ × 6) ÷ 100

⇒ 1,260 = 28 × R₂ × 6

⇒ 1,260 = 168 × R₂

⇒ R₂ = 1,260 ÷ 168

⇒ R₂ = 7.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Property

If the simple interest and principal remain constant, the rate of interest is inversely proportional to the time period (R ∝ 1/T).

Total Amount in SI

The total amount (A) is the sum of Principal and Interest: A = P + (P × R × T)/100 = P(1 + RT/100).

SI vs CI Difference

Simple interest is calculated only on the principal, whereas compound interest is calculated on the principal plus the accumulated interest of previous periods.

questions.question: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 70 kg and 35 kg is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Weights of the family members = 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 70 kg, 35 kg.

**Formula Used:**

Average weight = (Sum of all weights) / (Number of members)

**Calculation:**

Sum of all weights = 40 + 49 + 56 + 70 + 35

Sum of all weights = 250

Number of members = 5

Average weight = 250 / 5

⇒ Average weight = 50 kg

**The average weight of the family members is 50 kg.**

Initial quantity of water = (3/10) × 60 = 18 litres

New quantity of water = 18 + 3 = 21 litres

New ratio = 2 : 1

questions.question: The ratio of income to expenditure of a family is 18:15. Find the savings if the income of the family is ₹81,000.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Income to expenditure ratio = 18:15

Income of the family = ₹81,000

**Formula Used:**

Savings = Income - Expenditure

**Calculation:**

Let the common ratio factor be x.

Income = 18x

Expenditure = 15x

Given Income = ₹81,000

⇒ 18x = 81,000

⇒ x = 81,000 / 18

⇒ x = 4,500

Expenditure = 15x

⇒ Expenditure = 15 × 4,500

⇒ Expenditure = ₹67,500

Savings = Income - Expenditure

⇒ Savings = ₹81,000 - ₹67,500

⇒ Savings = ₹13,500

**The savings of the family is ₹13,500.**

questions.question: The curved surface area of a cylinder is three-fifth of its total surface area. Find the ratio between the height and radius of the cylinder.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The curved surface area of a cylinder is three-fifth of its total surface area.

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cylinder = 2πrh

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a cylinder = 2πrh + 2πr²

CSA = (3/5) TSA

**Calculation:**

Let the radius of the cylinder be r and the height be h.

Given, CSA = (3/5) TSA

⇒ 2πrh = (3/5)(2πrh + 2πr²)

⇒ 2πrh = (6πrh + 6πr²)/5

⇒ 10πrh = 6πrh + 6πr²

⇒ 10rh = 6rh + 6r²

⇒ 4rh = 6r²

⇒ h/r = 6/4

⇒ h/r = 3/2

**The ratio between the height and radius of the cylinder is 3:2.**

The combined number of bicycles produced during 1996, 1997 and 2000 is what percentage (rounded off to 1 decimal place) of the combined bicycles produced from 1996 to 2000?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The number of bicycles produced in the years 1996, 1997, 1998, 1999, and 2000 are as follows:

1996: 900 bicycles

1997: 750 bicycles

1998: 1050 bicycles

1999: 875 bicycles

2000: 1250 bicycles

**Calculation:**

The combined number of bicycles produced in 1996, 1997, and 2000 is:

900 + 750 + 1250 = 2900 bicycles

The total number of bicycles produced from 1996 to 2000 is:

900 + 750 + 1050 + 875 + 1250 = 4825 bicycles

Now, the percentage of the combined bicycles produced in 1996, 1997, and 2000 is:

⇒ (2900)/(4825) times 100 = 60.10

**∴ The combined number of bicycles produced during 1996, 1997, and 2000 is approximately 60.1% of the total bicycles produced from 1996 to 2000.**

questions.question: A man sold an article for ₹247.50, thereby gaining 12.5%. The cost of the article (in ₹) was:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹247.50

Gain Percentage = 12.5%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = SP × 100 / (100 + Gain%)

**Calculation:**

Gain% = 12.5%

SP = ₹247.50

CP = 247.50 × 100 / (100 + 12.5)

CP = 247.50 × 100 / 112.5

CP = 24750 / 112.5

CP = 220

**The cost of the article is ₹220.**

questions.question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2000 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 4 years.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹2000

Rate of Interest (R) = 7% per year

Time (T) = 4 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P times R times T)/(100)

**Calculation:**

SI = ₹2000 × 7% × 4 years

SI = (2000 times 7 times 4)/(100)

SI = (56000)/(100)

SI = ₹560

**The simple interest is ₹560.**

questions.question: The average of the present ages of P and Q is 56 years and their ages are in the ratio 5:3. What will be the age of Q seven years hence?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average of the present ages of P and Q is 56 years.

The ratio of their ages is 5:3.

**Formula Used:**

If the ratio of ages is a:b, then the ages can be represented as ax and bx where x is a common multiplier.

**Calculation:**

Let the present ages of P and Q be 5x and 3x respectively.

Average age of P and Q = 56 years

(5x + 3x)/(2) = 56 

⇒ (8x)/(2) = 56

⇒ 4x = 56

⇒ x = 14

Present age of Q = 3x = 3 × 14 = 42 years

Age of Q seven years hence = 42 + 7 = 49 years

**The correct answer is option 4.**
